item.content:encoded:
I re-read it a few months later, and took in mind the "freaks my mind, man" analysis I had made months ago was wrong.

And I still don't get it. I don't understand what's happening under the second collapsible. It's either too much mathematics or I'm just incapable of mentally constructing a coherent image when given abstract details.

Twice "spacetime distortions" are mentioned, and both times, absolutely no explanation of what that even means is given. I'm not math good, so to me, "spacetime" is astrophysics and relativity. What I see instead is audio engineering, geometry, and sudden death for some reason.

When I said this wasn't a "Class of '76" item, I just meant that this iteration of the item wasn't recovered at Kirk Lonwood High School. I wanted to give Syncope a bit more history, but I didn't make it clear enough that this was still a Syncope item at first. Hopefully the edit to the Description clears that up.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
You know, I wanted to make the 'base' frequency 432Hz for that reason, but then I thought: what if the effect of SCP-814-1/2 is to "straighten out" local spacetime by using that slightly different base frequency? And so….

In terms of description of what's happening, there was a deliberate choice made to couch that in scientific terms. I removed some of that during the drafting process — this article no longer presumes that the reader knows what a Minkowski space is, for example — but I don't want to spell it out too clearly because that removes some of the "a-ha!" potential.

By the way, the only Easter egg in the frequencies, other than the choice of 440Hz as the base tone, is that they are factors of 4 apart, except 55Hz. And I picked that one, rather than 110Hz, because I imagined people with decent speakers trying it on tone generators to see what it sounded like, and then: bass!

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Okay! This is my rewrite of SCP-814, one of the site's classic articles. This article was originally posted way back on 25 Aug 2009 by kabu, and then edit-rewritten as "Sound of '76" by Roget on 23 Feb 2013. I hope I did justice to both the original author and the first rewriter. I tried to keep elements of both of their iterations in mine — the general effect from the original, and something of the "purest sound" concept from Roget's version — so as to remain faithful to the history of the article.

Edit: In this rewrite, this is totally still a Syncope item — albeit one was produced rather earlier than the '70s — so I've changed the article to make that a bit more obvious, as that appears to have been missed by a lot of people (mea culpa).
